resolution: The case does not choose between the two senses. Every premise that speaks of act (STMT-NOTHING-MOVES-EXCEPT-AS-IN-ACT, STMT-NOTHING-IN-ACT-AND-POTENCY-IN-SAME-RESPECT, STMT-PLURAL-FIRST-MOVERS-WOULD-DIFFER-IN-ACT, STMT-ACTUALITY-ONLY-INSOFAR-AS-BEING, STMT-FIRST-UNMOVED-MOVER-HAS-EVERY-PERFECTION) uses the one parameter `InAct`, so within a result every premise is read in the same sense and no step passes from one sense to the other. The choice matters for premise truth, not validity: read formally, 'a thing moves only as in act' faces causes that produce what they do not themselves have; read virtually, the non-simultaneity premise must hold for virtual act too. A defence of these premises must fix one sense and defend all of them in it.
